resources.title: Housing — Basel
resources.body: Basel offers relatively more affordable rents than Zurich or Geneva. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 1,699/month per Numbeo (Aug 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — Basel
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need a valid passport or ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung), and a residence/work permit (non-EU). Main banks in Basel: UBS and Basler Kantonalbank (BKB). Raiffeisen branches are also available. PostFinance serves the whole country.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Basel
resources.body: Basel's international community, driven by pharmaceutical companies (Novartis, Roche), supports several international schools. International School Basel (ISB) offers IB and American curricula. The Minerva School offers a Swiss Matura. The German-French border region also offers French lycée options.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Basel
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the Einwohnerdienste Basel-Stadt within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals register for permit B or L at the Amt für Migration Basel-Stadt. Non-EU nationals need a residence permit from the cantonal authority before or upon arrival. Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Basel
resources.body: The AHV-Nummer (OASI number) serves as the Swiss social insurance and tax reference number, assigned by the SVA Basel-Stadt (cantonal compensation office) or employer. Basel-Stadt levies cantonal income and wealth taxes; cross-border commuters from Germany/France may have specific tax treaties applying.

resources.title: Transport — Basel
resources.body: Basel's public transport is operated by BVB (Basler Verkehrs-Betriebe) and BLT (Baselland Transport), part of the TNW (Tarifverbund Nordwestschweiz) network. A monthly city zone pass costs approximately CHF 86 per Numbeo data. EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Motorfahrzeugkontrolle Basel-Stadt without a driving test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/OFSP.

resources.title: Housing — Bern
resources.body: Bern, Switzerland's capital, has moderate rent levels. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 1,551/month per Numbeo (Aug 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — Bern
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need valid ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung), and a residence/work permit (non-EU). Main banks in Bern: UBS and Bernische Kantonalbank (BEKB). PostFinance headquarters are in Bern; branches nationwide. Raiffeisen is also present.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Bern
resources.body: Bern has several international school options, including Bern International School (BIS) which is the main IB-accredited institution. The Swiss diplomatic and federal administration community sustains demand for bilingual education. The canton's public schools are German-language.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Bern
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the Einwohnerdienste Bern (residents' registration) within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals register for permit B or L at the Migrationsdienst Kanton Bern. Non-EU nationals need a permit from the cantonal authority. Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Bern
resources.body: The AHV-Nummer (OASI number) serves as the Swiss tax and social insurance ID, assigned by the SVA Bern (cantonal compensation office) or employer. Canton Bern has one of the higher cantonal tax burdens in Switzerland. Withholding tax (Quellensteuer) applies for foreign residents without a C-permit.

resources.title: Transport — Bern
resources.body: Bern's public transport is operated by BERNMOBIL (trams, buses) and RBS (regional rail), part of the Libero fare network. A monthly city zone pass costs approximately CHF 82 per Numbeo data. EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Strassenverkehrs- und Schifffahrtsamt (SVSA Bern) without a driving test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/OFSP.

resources.title: Housing — Geneva
resources.body: Geneva is one of Switzerland's most expensive rental markets. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 2,286/month per Numbeo (Aug 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — Geneva
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need a valid passport or ID, proof of Swiss residence registration, and (for non-EU) a residence/work permit. Main banks in Geneva: UBS and Banque Cantonale de Genève (BCGE). PostFinance serves the whole country. Many banks offer English-language services in Geneva due to the international community.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Geneva
resources.body: Geneva has a dense network of international schools reflecting its role as a hub for UN and international organisations. Notable schools include Geneva International School (GIS), Institut Florimont, and the International School of Geneva (Ecolint), offering IB, French Baccalaureate, and other curricula.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Geneva
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the Office cantonal de la population (OCP) in Geneva within 8 days of arrival (Geneva-specific rule, stricter than federal 14-day rule). EU/EFTA nationals receive permit B or L from the cantonal migration authority. Non-EU nationals need a permit from the Office cantonal de la population et des migrations (OCPM). Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Geneva
resources.body: AHV-Nummer (OASI number) is the Swiss social insurance and tax reference number, assigned by the cantonal AVS compensation office (OCAS Genève) or employer. 13-digit format (756.XXXX.XXXX.XX). Geneva also has an income tax withholding system (impôt à la source) for foreign residents without a C-permit.

resources.title: Transport — Geneva
resources.body: Geneva's public transport is operated by TPG (Transports Publics Genevois), offering trams, buses, and boats. A monthly city travel pass costs approximately CHF 75 per Numbeo data. EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Service des automobiles et de la navigation (SAN) in Geneva; no test required. Mandatory Krankenversicherung/assurance-maladie must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/OFSP.

resources.title: Housing — Lausanne
resources.body: Lausanne is a major Francophone hub on Lake Geneva. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 1,882/month per Numbeo (Sep 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — Lausanne
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need valid ID, proof of Swiss residence (attestation d'établissement), and permit if non-EU. Main banks in Lausanne: UBS and Banque Cantonale Vaudoise (BCV). PostFinance and Raiffeisen branches also operate locally.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Lausanne
resources.body: Lausanne has a well-established international school sector, partly driven by the Olympic Committee (IOC) headquarters and international organisations. Schools include Institut Le Rosey (nearby), Brillantmont International School, and École Nouvelle de la Suisse Romande. IB and French Baccalaureate are widely offered.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Lausanne
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the contrôle des habitants of their commune within 8 days of arriving in canton Vaud (stricter than federal 14-day rule). EU/EFTA nationals receive permit B or L from the cantonal migration office (Service de la population, SPOP). Non-EU nationals need a cantonal permit before arrival. Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Lausanne
resources.body: The AHV-Nummer (OASI number) is assigned by the cantonal compensation office (Caisse cantonale vaudoise de compensation, CCVD) or employer. Vaud applies cantonal income and wealth taxes. Foreign residents without a C-permit are subject to withholding tax (impôt à la source).

resources.title: Transport — Lausanne
resources.body: Lausanne's public transport is operated by TL (Transports Lausannois), including the famous metro (M2), buses and trolleybuses. A monthly pass costs approximately CHF 78 per Numbeo data. EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Service des automobiles (SAN VD) without a test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung (assurance-maladie) must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/OFSP.

resources.title: Housing — Lucerne
resources.body: Lucerne is a popular tourist and expat destination in central Switzerland. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 1,748/month per Numbeo (Aug 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — Lucerne
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need valid ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung), and permit (non-EU). Main banks in Lucerne: UBS, Luzerner Kantonalbank (LUKB), and Raiffeisen. PostFinance serves the whole country.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Lucerne
resources.body: Lucerne has a small but established international school sector. International School of Zug and Lucerne (ISZL) serves both cantons with IB curriculum. The canton's main schools operate in German. Given the tourism industry, bilingual options are increasing.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Lucerne
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the Einwohnerkontrolle of their Lucerne municipality within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals register for permit B or L at the Dienststelle Migration des Kantons Luzern. Non-EU nationals need a cantonal permit. Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Lucerne
resources.body: The AHV-Nummer (OASI number) serves as the Swiss tax and social insurance ID, assigned by the SVA Luzern (cantonal compensation office) or employer. Lucerne canton applies cantonal income and wealth taxes; rates are moderate compared to Zurich or Bern. Withholding tax applies for foreign residents without a C-permit.

resources.title: Transport — Lucerne
resources.body: Lucerne's public transport is operated by VBL (Verkehrsbetriebe Luzern), including buses and the Luzern S-Bahn (integrated into the ZVV-like luzern-verkehr.ch network). A monthly pass costs approximately CHF 80 per Numbeo data. EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Strassenverkehrsamt Kanton Luzern without a driving test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/OFSP.

resources.title: Housing — Lugano
resources.body: Lugano is the largest Italian-speaking Swiss city and a financial centre in Ticino. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 1,408/month per Numbeo (Aug 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — Lugano
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need valid ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (iscrizione anagrafica), and permit (non-EU). Main banks in Lugano: UBS and Banca Cantonale Ticinese (Banca dello Stato del Cantone Ticino, bancastato.ch). Lugano hosts several private and international banks given its financial services sector.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Lugano
resources.body: Lugano's Italian-speaking environment means local public schools follow Swiss Italian curriculum. International schools in Lugano include Lugano International School (LIS) offering IB, and several other private institutions. Cross-border proximity to Italy also provides access to Italian liceo options.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Lugano
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the Ufficio controllo abitanti of their Lugano municipality within 8 days of arrival in canton Ticino (stricter than federal 14-day rule). EU/EFTA nationals register for permit B or L at the Sezione della popolazione (cantonal migration office). Non-EU nationals need a cantonal permit. Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Lugano
resources.body: The AHV-Nummer (OASI number / numero AVS) serves as the Swiss tax and social insurance ID, assigned by the Cassa cantonale di compensazione (cantonal office in Ticino) or employer. Ticino has moderate cantonal tax rates. Cross-border workers (frontalieri) from Italy are subject to specific bilateral tax agreements. Withholding tax applies for foreign residents without a C-permit.

resources.title: Transport — Lugano
resources.body: Lugano's public transport is operated by TPL Lugano (Ticino Public Transport), including bus network and the Lugano funicular. A monthly zone pass costs approximately CHF 64 per Numbeo data. EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Sezione della circolazione (Lugano) without a driving test. Mandatory assicurazione malattia (Krankenversicherung) must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/UFSP.

resources.title: Housing — St. Gallen
resources.body: St. Gallen is Switzerland's largest city in the east and offers some of the most affordable rents among major Swiss cities. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 1,463/month per Numbeo (Jun 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — St. Gallen
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need valid ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung), and permit (non-EU). Main banks in St. Gallen: UBS and St. Galler Kantonalbank (SGKB). Raiffeisen has its headquarters in St. Gallen. PostFinance serves the whole country.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — St. Gallen
resources.body: St. Gallen has public German-language schools as the predominant option. For international education, the International School Rheintal (ISR) in nearby Buchs (Appenzell border) offers IB curriculum. The region also has bilingual private schools and the proximity to Germany and Austria means access to German Abitur pathways.

resources.title: Registration & admin — St. Gallen
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the Einwohnerkontrolle of their St. Gallen municipality within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals register for permit B or L at the Ausländeramt Kanton St. Gallen. Non-EU nationals need a cantonal permit. Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — St. Gallen
resources.body: The AHV-Nummer (OASI number) serves as the Swiss tax and social insurance ID, assigned by the SVA St. Gallen (cantonal compensation office) or employer. St. Gallen canton levies moderate cantonal income and wealth taxes. Withholding tax applies for foreign residents without a C-permit.

resources.title: Transport — St. Gallen
resources.body: St. Gallen's public transport is operated by VBSG (Verkehrsbetriebe St. Gallen), including trolleybuses and buses, integrated into the Ostwind fare network. A monthly zone pass costs approximately CHF 106 per Numbeo data (wider zone). EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Strassenverkehrsamt Kanton St. Gallen without a driving test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/OFSP.

resources.title: Housing — Winterthur
resources.body: Winterthur is Zurich canton's second city with more affordable rents than Zurich city. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 1,910/month per Numbeo (Jun 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — Winterthur
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need valid ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung), and permit (non-EU). Winterthur falls under Zurich canton; main banks are UBS, Zürcher Kantonalbank (ZKB), and Raiffeisen. PostFinance serves the whole country.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Winterthur
resources.body: Winterthur has public German-language schools as the main educational option. For international education, families typically commute to Zurich international schools. Some private bilingual schools exist in the greater Zurich/Winterthur area. Zurich International School (ZIS) has a campus relatively nearby.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Winterthur
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the Einwohnerkontrolle Winterthur within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals register for permit B or L at the Migrationsamt des Kantons Zürich. Non-EU nationals need a cantonal permit. Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Winterthur
resources.body: The AHV-Nummer (OASI number) serves as the Swiss tax and social insurance ID, assigned by the SVA Zürich (cantonal compensation office) or employer. Winterthur is in Zurich canton, which applies Zurich cantonal income and wealth taxes. Withholding tax applies for foreign residents without a C-permit.

resources.title: Transport — Winterthur
resources.body: Winterthur's public transport is operated by STADTBUS Winterthur and integrated into the ZVV (Zürcher Verkehrsverbund) network, including S-Bahn connections to Zurich. A monthly pass costs approximately CHF 79 per Numbeo data. EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Strassenverkehrsamt Zürich without a driving test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/OFSP.

resources.title: Housing — Zug
resources.body: Zug is Switzerland's wealthiest canton and has very high rents, driven by low taxes attracting corporations and high earners. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 3,180/month per Numbeo (Jun 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — Zug
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents need valid ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung), and permit (non-EU). Main banks in Zug: UBS, Zuger Kantonalbank (ZugerKB), and Raiffeisen. Zug is famous for attracting international blockchain and crypto companies, and specialist private banks operate locally.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Zug
resources.body: Zug has a strong international school sector. The International School of Zug and Lucerne (ISZL) is the main IB-accredited institution, serving international families. The canton's public schools are German-language. Several private and bilingual schools operate in the region.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Zug
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the Einwohnerkontrolle of their Zug municipality within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals register for permit B or L at the Amt für Migration Kanton Zug. Non-EU nationals need a cantonal permit. Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Zug
resources.body: The AHV-Nummer (OASI number) serves as the Swiss tax and social insurance ID, assigned by the SVA Zug (cantonal compensation office) or employer. Zug canton has Switzerland's lowest cantonal tax rates, making it a major draw for international businesses and wealthy individuals. Withholding tax applies for foreign residents without a C-permit.

resources.title: Transport — Zug
resources.body: Zug's public transport is operated by ZVB (Zugerland Verkehrsbetriebe), including buses and the Zug S-Bahn integrated into the cantons' network. A monthly pass costs approximately CHF 133 per Numbeo data (wider zone pass). EU/EFTA driving licences are exchangeable within 12 months at the Strassenverkehrsamt Kanton Zug without a driving test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung must be arranged within 3 months of arrival; regulated by BAG/OFSP.

resources.title: Housing — Zurich
resources.body: Zurich is Switzerland's most expensive rental market. Average 1-BR city-centre apartments run ~CHF 2,519/month per Numbeo (Aug 2026). Swiss law caps the rental deposit at 3 months' rent. Main portals: homegate.ch, comparis.ch, immoscout24.ch.

resources.title: Banking — Zurich
resources.body: To open a bank account in Switzerland, residents typically need a valid passport or national ID, proof of Swiss residence registration (Anmeldebestätigung), and sometimes a work permit or residence permit. UBS and Zürcher Kantonalbank (ZKB) are the main banks in Zurich. PostFinance is a nationwide option. Online account opening available at most banks.

resources.title: Schools & childcare — Zurich
resources.body: Zurich hosts numerous international schools offering IB, British, American and other curricula, including the International School of Zurich North, Zurich International School (ZIS), and Inter-Community School (ICS). The Swiss federation of international schools maintains a directory.

resources.title: Registration & admin — Zurich
resources.body: Newcomers must register at the Einwohnerkontrolle (residents' registration office) of their municipality within 14 days of arrival. EU/EFTA nationals register for a permit B (over 1 year) or L (under 1 year) at the Cantonal Migration Office. Non-EU nationals need a residence permit from the cantonal authority (Migrationsamt Zürich) before or upon arrival. Authority: sem.admin.ch.

resources.title: Tax & finance — Zurich
resources.body: Every employed or self-employed person in Switzerland receives an AHV-Nummer (OASI/AHV social security number), which also serves as the Swiss tax ID. It is assigned by the cantonal AHV compensation office or the employer upon commencement of employment. Zurich's cantonal authority is the SVA Zürich (svazurich.ch). The number is 13 digits (756.XXXX.XXXX.XX).

resources.title: Transport — Zurich
resources.body: Zurich's public transport is operated by ZVV (Zürcher Verkehrsverbund), encompassing trams, buses, S-Bahn, and boats. A monthly zone pass (zones 110+121, city area) costs approximately CHF 88 per Numbeo data. EU/EFTA driving licences can be exchanged at the Strassenverkehrsamt Zürich within 12 months of establishing residency without a driving test. Mandatory Krankenversicherung (basic health insurance) must be taken out within 3 months of arrival or gaining residency; regulated by the Federal Office of Public Health (BAG/OFSP) at bag.admin.ch.
